info.title: Aurix Voice Platform API
info.summary: Self-hosted low-latency game voice: control-plane REST API
info.description:
REST control plane of the Aurix voice platform. Real-time media never crosses this API: players talk to a node
over the WebSocket control plane (`/ws`, see the *WebSocket protocol* chapter of the docs) and stream audio over
native AURX/UDP or WebRTC.

## Authentication

| Caller | Credential | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| Your game backend | **API key** — `X-API-Key: aurx_…` or `Authorization: Bearer aurx_…` | everything under `/v1/*` except `/v1/me/*`, `/v1/webrtc/*`, `/v1/apps*`, `/v1/nodes` |
| Player (game client) | **Session JWT** from `POST /v1/tokens` — `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | `/v1/me/*`, `/v1/webrtc/offer`, the WebSocket |
| Operator | **Admin JWT** from `POST /admin/login` — `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | `/admin/*`, `/v1/apps*`, `/v1/nodes` |
| First run | `X-Bootstrap-Token` (or no admins yet) | `POST /admin/setup` |

Every API-key and player route is scoped to the **application (tenant) of the credential**; ids from other
applications behave as if they did not exist (`404`). API keys carry a permission list — each operation
documents what it needs in `x-aurix-permissions` (`*` grants everything). Admin-only operations that require the
`superadmin` role say so in `x-aurix-admin-role`.

Known permissions: `*`, `tokens:issue`, `turn:issue`, `channels:read`, `channels:write`, `users:read`, `users:write`, `users:erase`, `users:export`, `moderation:read`, `moderation:write`, `recordings:read`, `recordings:write`, `audio_streams:read`, `audio_streams:write`, `chat:read`, `chat:write`, `tts:write`, `keys:manage`, `analytics:read`, `audit:read`, `webhooks:read`, `webhooks:write`, `events:read`.

## Errors

Non-2xx responses use one envelope: `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}`. Codes map to statuses as
follows: authentication → `401`; missing permission, action-token, ban or server-mute refusals → `403`;
unknown or foreign-tenant ids (and chat/TTS when disabled) → `404`; quota, channel-full and other conflicts →
`409`; validation → `400`; a chat message rejected by the filter → `422`; rate limit (per IP or per key, fleet-wide) → `429`
(`Retry-After` is set); features not configured on this deployment → `501`; speech-provider failures → `502`;
no media node available → `503`; provider timeouts → `504`.

## Conventions

* Identifiers are UUIDs, timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
* Lists that paginate take `page` (from 1) and `per_page` and return `{data, page, per_page, total}` unless
  documented otherwise.
* Some resources are **node-local** (session stats, live audio streams): behind a load balancer, address the
  node that hosts the session/channel (it is listed in `GET /v1/users/{user_id}`).
* Secrets (API keys, webhook secrets, TURN passwords) appear exactly once, in the response that creates them.

post.description: Applies the `[retention]` rules immediately. The sweep holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock so only one node runs it at a time.
Returns the application's first API key with all permissions; it is shown only once.

patch.description: Fields left out are unchanged; `description: null` clears it. Raising `max_participants_per_channel` is how an existing application gets large (audience) channels — `POST /v1/channels` clamps `config.max_participants` to this quota. Lowering it affects channels created or reconfigured afterwards.

get.description: Every node registers itself and heartbeats; nodes silent for 30 s are marked unhealthy.

post.description: Creates or looks up the user by `external_id` and returns a session JWT with the channel grants. Call this from your game backend; never ship API keys to clients.

`login` opens a session, `join` enters one channel, `kick`/`mute`/`unmute` authorise a single moderation act (these three additionally need `moderation:write`). Each token is bound to a `jti` that is consumed atomically on first use. With `auth.require_action_tokens = true` session JWTs alone can no longer open sessions or join channels.

get.summary: Region discovery for the game backend
get.description: One entry per region with at least one healthy, non-saturated node that advertises a public WebSocket URL, carrying that region's least-loaded node. Use it to choose the region before minting a token, or pass `region`/`location` straight to `POST /v1/tokens` and read `endpoint`. Served from the node registry, which follows the fleet's heartbeats with at most ~15 s of lag.

parameters.description: Only messages older than this cursor. Opaque keyset cursor (`(sent_at, id)`, URL-safe base64) taken from a previous page's `next_before` / `next_after` or from a message's position; equal timestamps never skip or repeat a row. Invalid cursors are `400`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only messages newer than this cursor (walk forward from a known position). Opaque keyset cursor (`(sent_at, id)`, URL-safe base64) taken from a previous page's `next_before` / `next_after` or from a message's position; equal timestamps never skip or repeat a row. Invalid cursors are `400`.

They are moderation events with `event_type` `safety.voice` or `safety.text` (so `POST /v1/moderation/events/{event_id}/resolve` closes them); `evidence` holds the score, categories, flagged text, classifier and lexicon verdicts, context messages and the evidence-clip metadata. Newest first.

parameters.description: Only incidents of this user.

get.description: The incident with its context messages and, for voice incidents with a stored clip, the recording metadata and the path that streams it (`recordings:read`).

get.summary: Export an incident with its evidence
get.description: Self-contained JSON bundle for hand-off to a trust & safety team: the incident, the surrounding chat messages and — when a clip exists **and the key also holds `recordings:read`** — the decrypted Ogg/Opus audio inline as `audio.content_base64`. Reading the clip is written to the audit log as `recording.accessed`. Without `recordings:read` the bundle is returned without the audio bytes.

Decayed sum of the user's recent incident scores (`[safety].risk_half_life_secs`), the same value that drives automatic mute/kick triggers and `safety.risk_changed` events. Computed from stored incidents, identical on every node.

get.description: Hash-chained; every privileged action (keys, bans, kicks, recording access, …) is recorded.

post.description: Requires `recording.enabled` on the node and the participant to be live on it. With `recording.require_consent` audio is written only after the participant accepts the `RecordingNotification`.

session_id.description: Disambiguates when the user has several sessions.

get.summary: Recording metadata, download URL and consent state

download_url.description: Pre-signed URL (15 min) when the store is S3 and the recording is `ready`; `null` for local storage — use the `download` route.

delete.summary: Delete a recording and its file

get.description: Decrypted on the fly when recording encryption is enabled. Access is written to the audit log. Participant tracks and Opus mixdowns are Ogg/Opus, WAV mixdowns are 16-bit PCM. 409 while the recording is still `recording`/`processing` or has `failed`.

get.summary: Live streams of this application on this node

post.description: Aurix connects to your WebSocket endpoint and pushes per-participant Opus or PCM frames (36-byte binary header) plus JSON control frames. Streams are node-local: address the node that hosts participants of the channel (`409` otherwise).

get.summary: Live streams of a channel on this node

get.description: Not a plain HTTP call: upgrade to WebSocket with the API key in `X-API-Key` / `Authorization`. Frames flow once the socket is open and the stream ends when it closes. Streams are node-local: address the node that hosts participants of the channel (`409` otherwise).

parameters.name: users
parameters.description: Comma-separated user ids to include (default: everyone).

200.description: Final state of the stopped stream

post.description: The response includes `secret` (once). Deliveries are `POST`s with the `EventEnvelope` body and `X-Aurix-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<body>"))`; failures retry from 5 s up to 2 h.

get.summary: Server-sent event stream for this application
get.description: `text/event-stream`. Opens with `event: stream.open`, then one `event: <type>` per `EventEnvelope` (`id` = event id) and periodic keepalive comments. `event: lagged` means the consumer fell behind and events were dropped — fetch `/v1/events/snapshot` to resynchronise. High-frequency types (`participant.typing`, `participant.speaking`, `channel.energy`) are sent only when listed in `types`.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated event types (default: everything except the high-frequency ones).

post.description: The reporter is the authenticated player.

post.summary: Answer a recording consent request over REST
post.description: Equivalent to the WebSocket `RecordingConsentResponse`; only the recorded participant may answer.
Alternative to the WebSocket `WebRtcOffer` message. The session must have been opened over the WebSocket by the same player; the SDP is limited to 64 KiB.

post.summary: Render a channel mixdown from participant tracks
post.description: Combines finished per-participant tracks of one channel (aligned on `audio_started_at`, summed with soft clipping) into a single Ogg/Opus or WAV file. Returns the new recording with `kind = mixdown` and `status = processing`; it becomes `ready` asynchronously — poll `GET /v1/recordings/{id}` or subscribe to `recording.processed`. The job runs on the node that accepted the request, which must be able to read every source (its own files or object storage); otherwise 409 names the node holding the track. 429 when this node's processing queue (`recording.processing.max_queued`) is full.

sources.description: Tracks to combine (all `kind = recording`, `status = ready`, same channel; at most `recording.processing.max_sources`). Omitted or empty — every finished track of the channel.

stereo.description: Render two channels (stereo tracks keep L/R; mono tracks are centred).

post.summary: Queue speech-to-text of a stored recording
post.description: Requires an `[stt]` provider on the node. A participant track is transcribed as one speaker; a mixdown is transcribed from its source tracks one by one, so every segment names its speaker. Audio is decoded in `recording.processing.stt_chunk_secs` chunks cut on silence and resampled to `stt_sample_rate`. Returns the transcript row with `status = queued`; poll `GET .../transcript` or wait for `recording.processed` with `job = transcript`. 409 while a transcript of this recording is already queued/running or the recording is not `ready`; a `failed` transcript may be requested again.

get.summary: Transcript of a recording (JSON, SRT or WebVTT)
get.description: `format=json` (default) returns the row in any state; `srt`/`vtt` render the segments as subtitles (speaker as a `<v uuid>` voice tag) and require `status = ready` (409 otherwise).

With `channel_id` or `peer_user_id`: the user's marker in that conversation (`null` if they never read there) and how many messages from others lie after it (capped at `chat.unread_count_cap`). Without a selector: every marker of the user. Requires `chat.persist = true` (otherwise `404`).

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: Channel conversation (mutually exclusive with `peer_user_id`).

parameters.name: peer_user_id
parameters.description: Direct conversation with this user (mutually exclusive with `channel_id`).

put.description: Marks everything in the conversation up to `message_id` as read on the user's behalf (for example after a support agent answered for them). Markers only move forward: an older or equal position is accepted but `moved` is `false`. The message must belong to the selected conversation of that user, otherwise `404`. Every device of the user receives `ChatReadMarker`; with `chat.read_receipts` so do the channel members / the peer. Requires `chat.persist = true`.

get.description: Reading position of every user who marked something read in the channel (newest position first). Requires `chat.persist = true` (otherwise `404`).

ApiKeyBearer.description: The same API key as a bearer token.

BootstrapToken.name: X-Bootstrap-Token
BootstrapToken.description: `auth.bootstrap_token`; only for `POST /admin/setup` once an admin exists.

Forbidden.description: Credential lacks the permission, or the action is refused (ban, mute, action token)

NotFound.description: Unknown id, or the resource belongs to another application

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded — per client IP or per API key, enforced fleet-wide (`Retry-After` set)

user_id.description: Acting user (or use `external_id` + `display_name` to create/resolve one).

ad_hoc.description: `join` only: create the channel on first join.

jti.description: One-time id; the token is consumed atomically on first use.

AdHocChannel.description: Creates (or revives) a channel with a deterministic per-app id on the first join; the channel is removed when the last participant leaves.

key_prefix.description: First characters of the key, for identification only.

rate_limit.description: Requests per minute across the whole fleet (`0` = unlimited; the per-IP limit still applies).

actor_id.description: API key id, admin id or user id that performed the action.

previous_hash.description: Hash chain — each row commits to the previous one.

moderator_user_id.description: Attributed moderator (defaults to the API key).

created.description: Present on add: `false` if the block already existed.

removed.description: Present on remove: `false` if there was nothing to remove.

ad_hoc.description: Created on first join from a token grant; soft-deleted when the last participant leaves.

bitrate.description: Target uplink Opus bitrate in bit/s (also the ceiling server-driven adaptation returns to). Capped by the node's `media.max_bitrate`.

min_bitrate.description: Floor for server-driven bitrate adaptation (bit/s); must not exceed `bitrate`.

enable_dtx.description: Allow discontinuous transmission (silence frames are not sent).

enable_fec.description: Require in-band forward error correction on the uplink.

complexity.description: Encoder complexity hint 0..=10 (`null`: the client's default). Browsers ignore it.

ambient.description: Cocktail-party mode; absent/`null` (default) delivers every audible speaker at full gain.

audience.description: Large-channel / audience mode: hidden listeners, server mix for listeners, speaker admission cap, per-receiver stream cap. Absent/`null` (default): plain channel.

stereo.description: Participants may send two-channel (stereo) Opus (music, DJ, broadcast sources); delivered to clients as `audio.stereo`. Off: clients encode mono. The SFU forwards either; stereo receivers keep the image, mono receivers and server-side recording/STT downmix. Recordings started while this is on are written with a 2-channel OpusHead.

transcription.description: Transcribe speech (when `[stt]` is configured on the node) and deliver `Transcript` events.

safety_voice.description: Send the speakers' transcripts to the `[safety]` classifier (requires `[stt]`); disclosed to clients as `ChannelJoinAck.safety_voice`. Independent of `transcription`.

ChannelConfig.description: All fields are optional; omitted ones take the defaults shown. The Opus fields become the `AudioPolicy` delivered to participants in `ChannelJoinAck.audio` (and `ChannelAudioPolicy` on live edits).

OpusBandwidth.description: Widest audio bandwidth participants may encode (4/6/8/12/20 kHz).

channel_id.description: Existing channel; omit when `ad_hoc` is set.

live_on_this_node.description: Sessions whose media is handled by the node that answered.

ChannelType.description: `positional` — 3D attenuated/directional audio (requires `positional_config`); `team` — plain conference; `command` — only `command_speakers` transmit; `whisper` — one-to-one with `whisper_target`; `echo` — every participant hears only themselves (loopback test).

offline.description: Directed message accepted while the recipient had no live session; it was stored for replay when they connect. Omitted when `false`.

ChatMessage.description: Same shape as the WebSocket `ChatMessage`; `client_ref` is never part of history.

CoordinateSystem.description: Left-handed: Unity / Unreal. Right-handed: OpenGL, Three.js, Godot.

permissions.description: Subset of the known permissions (`*` = all). A key can only grant what it holds itself.

rate_limit.description: Requests per minute across the fleet; default 6000, `0` = unlimited.

mode.description: Only `push` can be created over REST; `pull` streams are opened with the WebSocket endpoint.

url.description: `wss://` endpoint Aurix connects to (`ws://` only outside production; private addresses are rejected).
`https://` in production; private/loopback addresses are rejected and redirects are not followed.

key.description: Shown exactly once — store it now.

api_key.description: First API key of the app (all permissions). Shown once.

Error.description: Every non-2xx response carries this envelope. `code` is stable and meant for programmatic handling; `message` is a sanitised, human-readable summary (internal details are never leaked).

id.description: Stable per event — reuse it for idempotent processing across retries.

data.description: Event-specific fields; `app_id` is lifted to the envelope.

EventEnvelope.description: Body of every webhook POST and `data` of every SSE event.

external_id.description: Your stable player id; the Aurix `user_id` is created/looked up from it.

region.description: Region the game wants the player in (e.g. the match's region). Wins in `endpoint` when it has capacity.

location.description: Player's approximate coordinates from the game's own geo data, used to order regions by distance.

push_url.description: Push mode only; credentials in the URL are redacted.

address.description: Public IPv4 (or host name) of the node's media socket (`media.external_ip`).

address_ipv6.description: Public IPv6 of the media socket when the node is dual-stack or IPv6-only (`media.external_ipv6`); `null` on IPv4-only nodes and nodes older than this schema.

ws_url.description: Public WebSocket URL advertised for region discovery; `null` when the node is not advertised.

NetworkQuality.description: Merged view of the client's `QualityReport` and the SFU's uplink measurements; the worse direction decides the rating (`R ≥ 80 → 5 bars, ≥ 70 → 4, ≥ 60 → 3, ≥ 50 → 2, else 1`).

Pagination.description: Offset pagination envelope used by list endpoints (`page` starts at 1, `per_page` is capped server-side).

max_radius.description: Beyond this distance nothing is delivered.

directional.description: Pan by the listener's orientation (stereo downlink).

roster_radius.description: Presence scope: members appear in each other's roster (join ack, `ParticipantJoined`/`Left`, positions, mute/speaking/energy) only when both positions are known and within this distance; leaving uses a 10 % wider radius. `null`: the whole channel.

text_radius.description: Text scope: channel chat, typing and transcripts reach only members within this distance of the sender (both positions known); the sender always gets their own echo. `null`: the whole channel.

max_voices.description: How many of the loudest concurrent speakers each receiver hears at full gain.

ambient_gain.description: Gain applied to every other concurrent speaker (`0` drops them).

AmbientConfig.description: Cocktail-party mixing, ranked per receiver by delivery gain × the sender-reported audio level (sticky slots, 400 ms hold).

hide_listeners.description: Receive-only members (role `listener`) are absent from the roster and presence notifications of other members; `ChannelJoinAck.participant_count` still carries the real headcount.

mix_for_listeners.description: Native listeners receive one server-mixed stream (`DownlinkMode.mixed`) whatever their own downlink mode. Browsers are always mixed.

max_speakers.description: Members that may speak the channel admits at once; `0` = only `max_participants` applies. Must not exceed `max_participants`.

max_streams.description: Concurrent voices a receiver hears at once (`0` = unlimited), ranked per receiver by delivery gain × sender level with sticky slots; bounds the streams a native client decodes, the tracks a browser receives and the voices a server mix decodes.

QualityMetrics.description: Last `QualityReport` the client sent (loss in percent).

session_id.description: Session of the recorded participant; the nil UUID for a mixdown.

user_id.description: Recorded participant for `kind = recording`/`evidence`; the nil UUID for a mixdown.

format.description: `ogg_opus` for participant tracks and Opus mixdowns, `wav` for PCM mixdowns.

expires_at.description: Retention deadline; the file is removed afterwards.

kind.description: `recording` — per-participant track; `evidence` — safety clip; `mixdown` — channel file rendered from tracks (`sources`).

status.description: `recording` while audio is being captured, `processing` while a mixdown renders, `ready` when the file can be downloaded, `failed` (see `error`).

audio_started_at.description: When the first audio was written (consent may delay it past `started_at`); tracks are aligned on it in mixdowns.

sources.description: Tracks a mixdown was rendered from.

node_id.description: Node that holds the file locally (irrelevant with object storage).

media_node_id.description: Node hosting the session (`GET /v1/nodes`, `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/stats` is node-local).

media_path.description: Wire path the media currently takes: native AURX over UDP, native AURX tunneled through the control WebSocket (UDP-blocked fallback), or WebRTC.

SweepReport.description: Rows removed by the retention sweep, per rule.

token.description: Session JWT — pass it to the SDK / WebSocket `SessionInit`.

endpoint.description: Recommended node for this player (preferred `region` → nearest to `location` → least loaded). Hand `ws_url` to the client together with the token; `null` when no node advertises a public WebSocket URL, in which case clients use your configured URL.

uris.description: `turn:` (UDP and TCP) and `stun:` URIs for every public address family of the node — IPv4 first, then IPv6 with the host bracketed (`turn:[2001:db8::10]:3478?transport=udp`). Pass them all to the ICE agent.

recordings_removed.description: Recording files/objects deleted from the store.

session_id.description: Session opened over the WebSocket by the same player.

secret.description: Only present in the create and rotate-secret responses.

Region.description: Deployment region label configured per node (`server.region`).

RegionEndpoint.description: The least-loaded healthy node of one region that advertises a public WebSocket URL (`server.external_ws_url`). Connect the SDK to `ws_url`; `GET probe_url` is a cheap public request answered by exactly this node, so its round-trip time is a fair RTT estimate.

ws_url.description: WebSocket control-plane URL of the node (`wss://…/ws`). Session resume must reach the same node, so this is a per-node URL, not a load balancer.

probe_url.description: `<api_url>/health` of the node, for client-side RTT measurement.

distance_km.description: Great-circle distance from the caller's declared location, when both are known.

nodes.description: Healthy, non-saturated nodes advertising a WebSocket URL in this region.

regions.description: Best-first: the preferred region if it has capacity, then by distance to the declared location (regions without coordinates last), then by load. Clients that can measure RTT should probe every `probe_url` and pick the lowest; this order is the fallback.

recommended.description: First entry of `regions`, or `null` when no node advertises a WebSocket URL.

RiskLevel.description: `elevated` / `high` are the configurable thresholds `[safety].risk_elevated` / `risk_high`; `low` is anything above zero.

incidents.description: Incidents inside the scoring window (10 half-lives).

SafetyIncidentAudio.description: Evidence clip stored as a recording of kind `evidence` (same encryption, object storage and retention sweep as recordings).

text.description: The flagged transcript or message (original, unmasked).

context.description: Messages delivered in the same channel / conversation before the flagged one (text incidents, `[safety.text].context_messages`).

content_base64.description: Present when the key holds `recordings:read` and the clip has not expired.

max_participants_per_channel.description: Upper bound for `ChannelConfig.max_participants` of this app's channels.

rate_limit.description: Requests per minute across the fleet; `0` = unlimited.

RecordingTranscript.description: Post-hoc speech-to-text of a stored recording. Segments carry the speaker (`user_id` of the source track) and offsets on the recording's timeline.

provider.description: Name of the STT provider that produced the text.

text.description: All segments in timeline order, space-joined.

speaker.description: User whose track this segment was recognised from.

words.description: Word timings when the provider returns them, shifted onto the recording timeline.

ChatHistoryPage.description: One page of chat history, newest first.

next_before.description: Cursor of the oldest message on the page; pass as `before` to get older ones. Absent when the page reached the oldest message.

next_after.description: Cursor of the newest message on the page; pass as `after` to get newer ones. Absent when the page reached the present.

ChatReadMarker.description: A user's reading position in one conversation: everything at or before `message_id` (ordered by `(message_sent_at, message_id)`) counts as read. Exactly one of `channel_id` / `peer_user_id` is set.

marker.description: `null` when the user never read in that conversation.

unread_count.description: Messages from others after the marker, capped at `chat.unread_count_cap`.
